Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zukomp (development version)

The next release is 0.2.0: it adds codecs, which is a feature rather than a fix.

The ZIP reader in libzukomp.a

  • For packages linking the static library (zuxlsx): miniz’s ZIP reader now refuses, with an mz_zip_error, four hostile archives it used to mishandle (#92). Reading a deflated member from an archive in memory through the extraction iterator no longer hangs when the member’s DEFLATE stream is cut short. mz_zip_reader_extract_to_mem() no longer reads past a stored entry whose two sizes differ. A corrupt DEFLATE stream now sets MZ_ZIP_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED instead of leaving the error at MZ_ZIP_NO_ERROR. An entry with no compressed data is checked as the iterator checks it (local header, method, size, CRC-32) instead of being returned as empty. And an archive whose central directory sits more than 4 KiB from its end, behind a long archive comment, now opens instead of being refused. Found by a new fuzz target and a comparison with Python’s zipfile (#37). A consumer gets the fix when it is reinstalled.

New codecs

  • zstd, lz4-frame and lz4-block are built in, from vendored zstd 1.5.7 and lz4 1.10.0 (#55). They were planned as separate satellite packages; both libraries are small, C and BSD-licensed, and every consumer wants both, so they ship in the core instead. Their codec ids (17, 18, 19) are the ones reserved for them, and komp_codecs() now reports all three as available.
  • codec = "auto" and komp_detect() recognise zstd (28 b5 2f fd) and LZ4 frames (04 22 4d 18). lz4-block has no header and, like deflate-raw, must be named.
  • Several zstd or LZ4 frames back to back decode as one stream, as several gzip members do; skippable frames are stepped over, and anything else after the last frame is zukomp_trailing_bytes.
  • Levels are codec-native: zstd takes -131072 to 22 (default 3, "fast" 1, "best" 19), and both LZ4 codecs take liblz4’s scale, -65536 to 12 (default and "fast" 1, "best" 12), where negative levels are acceleration.
  • zstd and LZ4 frames carry a content checksum, which decoding verifies; a mismatch is zukomp_checksum_error. A frame cut short is zukomp_truncated, because unlike a DEFLATE body these formats let the decoder tell “needs more” from “is wrong”.
  • max_output bounds zstd’s decoder window too: a frame header claiming a window larger than max_output allows (never less than 8 MiB) is refused as zukomp_output_limit before anything is allocated.
  • komp_info()$vendored lists zstd and lz4, and komp_info()$build_flags their trim.

C API

  • zu_decoder_opts gains expected_size, read when flags has the new ZU_DEC_EXPECTED_SIZE: the exact decoded size, for a caller that knows it from outside the stream (an Arrow IPC body’s length prefix, a Parquet page header). The core holds every codec to it, like max_output: output beyond it, or a stream ending short of it, is ZU_ERR_INVALID_DATA. lz4-block uses it to decode in one pass; without it the decoder has to search for the size under max_output. The field is appended, so consumers built against 0.1.0’s header are unaffected and ZUKOMP_ABI_VERSION stays 1.
  • Encoder and decoder handles follow one specified lifecycle, enforced by the core for every codec (#71). This changes behaviour that was unspecified, for C consumers only; no function, type or enum value changed.
    • A stream’s first error is sticky: every later zu_*_process() returns the same status and moves neither cursor until a reset. Before, the DEFLATE codecs repeated their error, zstd and lz4-frame returned a different one per call and then decoded fresh input, and after an expected-size, trailing-data or output-limit failure every codec answered ZU_STREAM_END on the next call (#83).
    • ZU_RUN or ZU_FLUSH after a call that passed ZU_FINISH is refused with ZU_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT, and the stream carries on. Before, the codecs disagreed: the DEFLATE encoders failed with invalid data, LZ4 ended the frame and dropped the new input, and zstd took it.
    • Input to a decoder after ZU_STREAM_END is ZU_ERR_TRAILING, and a failure, when ZU_DEC_REJECT_TRAILING is set, whichever call it arrives in.
    • A call refused before the stream sees it (a bad buffer, ZU_FLUSH on a codec that cannot flush) changes nothing, and a reset the codec fails leaves the handle failed.
  • src_pos is documented as exact at the end of a stream, with one exception: under ZU_DEC_CONCAT_MEMBERS, when the next member’s or frame’s magic straddles a buffer boundary, up to one byte (gzip) or three (zstd, lz4-frame) may be counted that turn out not to be a magic (#79). Decoding without the flag gives the exact end.

Bug fixes

  • The drive loop behind komp_compress() and komp_decompress() created its stream handle before the external pointer that owns it, so a longjmp while allocating that pointer leaked the handle. The owner is created first now (#78).

  • A zstd decoder handle that was called 16 times in a row without moving a byte (waiting for input, or for output room) reported its valid stream as ZU_ERR_INVALID_DATA. That was libzstd’s guard against a spinning caller, which is not an error in the stream; such calls now answer ZU_NEED_INPUT or ZU_NEED_OUTPUT however many there are (#100).

  • deflate-raw, zlib and gzip refuse the codes RFC 1951 reserves: the literal/length symbols 286 and 287 and the distance symbols 30 and 31, which a fixed-Huffman block can still carry, and a dynamic block header that declares more than 286 literal/length or 30 distance codes. miniz decoded a reserved symbol as an empty match or a distance of 0, so a malformed deflate-raw stream came back as data, and zlib and gzip delivered bytes before failing on the checksum (#94). The fix is a new local miniz patch, 0006-reject-reserved-codes.patch.

  • A truncated deflate-raw, zlib or gzip stream delivers the same bytes before its error whichever call carries ZU_FINISH. When it came with the final bytes, miniz stopped short of output it had already decoded (#68).

  • lz4-block gives a block one verdict whatever the limits. If the block breaks the format’s end-of-block rules (the last 5 bytes are literals, and the last match starts at least 12 bytes from the end), it is now always zukomp_invalid_data. The size search used to accept such a block, or call it zukomp_output_limit when max_output was its size (#93).

  • A zstd frame that declares its content size and ends in an empty last block is held to that size. libzstd’s streaming decoder skipped the check there, so such a frame decoded as empty when it arrived in chunks smaller than its declared size, and was refused otherwise (#68). The fix is a local zstd patch, 0002-check-content-size-after-empty-last-block.patch.

  • A valid zstd frame with a zero-byte window – single segment, declared content size 0 – ending in an RLE block of size 0 decodes at every chunk size. libzstd’s streaming decoder compared the RLE block’s one-byte body, not its size, with the frame’s maximum block size of 0, and called the frame corrupt whenever it arrived a few bytes at a time (#68). The fix is a local zstd patch, 0003-check-rle-block-size-not-body.patch.

  • A zstd compressed block of size 0 is zukomp_invalid_data at every chunk size. libzstd’s streaming decoder took it for an empty block, so a frame ending in one was a checksum failure, or accepted, when it arrived in small chunks (#68). The fix is a local zstd patch, 0004-refuse-empty-compressed-block.patch.

  • The deflate-raw, zlib and gzip decoders no longer reject a valid stream that ends exactly at max_output (as zukomp_output_limit) or at ZU_DEC_EXPECTED_SIZE (as zukomp_invalid_data) when an input chunk ends after the last output byte but before the end-of-block code or the trailer (#64). komp_decompress() passes its input in 64 KiB slices, so it could meet this only with a longer stream; streaming consumers of the C API met it at ordinary chunk sizes.

  • A DEFLATE block whose code table gives the end-of-block symbol no code is now zukomp_invalid_data before any output, however its bytes arrive (#74). miniz decoded such a block’s literals instead, so at small input chunks it produced output until max_output stopped it with zukomp_output_limit, and without a cap it never stopped. A fourth local miniz patch, 0004-reject-missing-end-of-block.patch, adds the check zlib makes.

  • The lz4-block decoder no longer applies the compressor’s input ceiling (LZ4_MAX_INPUT_SIZE, about 2 GiB of uncompressed bytes) to a compressed block, which for incompressible data is larger (#77). It takes blocks up to liblz4’s own limit, 2^31 - 1 bytes; a larger one is zukomp_unsupported_codec.

  • deflate-raw, zlib and gzip no longer silently truncate an input longer than 2^31 - 1 bytes passed in one call, which every komp_compress() is (#73). miniz was told the first 2^31 - 1 bytes were the whole input, and wrote a valid stream of that prefix with a matching checksum, so nothing downstream could tell. An encoder that ends its stream with input unread is now an internal error, for every codec.

  • zu_compress_bound() for lz4-frame no longer returns a tiny bound for sizes from 2^48 bytes, where liblz4’s block count wrapped; those sizes are refused (#85).

  • komp_decompress() rejects bytes after the stream as zukomp_trailing_bytes wherever the stream ends. A stream that ended on a 64 KiB input boundary was accepted with whatever followed it dropped (#90).

  • ZU_FLUSH on a deflate-raw, zlib or gzip encoder returns once the bytes so far are out. It used to fill all the output room it was given with empty stored blocks, so a C caller flushing until the encoder stopped asking for room never finished (#91).

  • On a 32-bit platform, a DEFLATE stream decoding to more than 4 GiB through one decoder no longer fails part way with zukomp_invalid_data: the history count in miniz patch 0002 saturates at the window instead of wrapping (#86).

Other changes

  • max_ratio is documented as what it has always been: a bound on expansion as decoding proceeds, checked against the compressed bytes read so far, not only on the final ratio (#80). A stream whose start is far more compressible than the rest can be refused although its overall ratio is under the limit.

  • komp_compress() passes the whole input to the codec in one call, so zstd and LZ4 frames record the content size and zstd sizes its tables to the input. Output for the DEFLATE family is unchanged.

  • The licences of the bundled zstd and lz4 are installed under licenses/, beside miniz’s, and LICENSE.note summarises all three.

zukomp 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-10-16

First release of the v1 feature set: a codec registry with a uniform byte-in/byte-out API, one vendored codec family, and a stable C ABI.

R API

  • komp_compress() and komp_decompress(), over identity, deflate-raw, zlib and gzip. Raw vectors only — encoding is the caller’s decision, so character input is refused.

  • komp_detect() and codec = "auto". Detection is a registry property, and it refuses to guess: headerless formats return NA and must be named, because guessing wrong there returns wrong bytes rather than an error.

  • komp_codecs(), the capability table. It also lists the codec names zukomp reserves for future implementations (zstd, brotli, …) with available = FALSE; none has been released yet, and asking for one is a zukomp_unsupported_codec error that says so. Its columns include can_flush, and level_fast/level_best — where the abstract level names land for each codec.

  • level accepts a codec-native whole number, NULL for the codec’s default, or one of the abstract names "fast", "default" and "best". Numeric levels are codec-native and deliberately not comparable between codecs, so the names are the portable way to say “compress harder”; they work on every codec, including ones with no level axis, where all three mean the codec’s one behaviour.

    The names are declared by each codec rather than derived from level_min/level_max, because the range is which integers are accepted, not which ones mean cheap and thorough: DEFLATE’s level 0 is stored blocks, and a codec whose level is an acceleration factor inverts the mapping entirely.

  • komp_codec_available() and komp_info(). komp_info()$version is a character string, so it pastes into a log line directly.

  • Structured conditions carrying codec, input_bytes, output_bytes and native_status, so callers branch on the class rather than on the message.

Safety

  • Decompression is capped at 1 GiB by default, overridable with options(zukomp.max_output = ). An optional max_ratio is off by default, since legitimately compressible data routinely exceeds any safe-looking threshold.
  • Both limits must be whole numbers. They are narrowed to integer types on the way to C, which truncates toward zero, and native 0 means no limit — so a fractional value in (0, 1) would otherwise disable the guard it was asked to impose. NULL, 0 and Inf are the spellings for unlimited.
  • Both limits are enforced by the core stream driver rather than by codecs, so a third-party codec inherits them and cannot bypass them.
  • Every checksum is verified, every truncation errors, and gzip’s ISIZE is validated against actual output — never used to size a buffer.
  • Trailing data after a gzip member is a trailing-data decision, never a malformed-member one. A following member is confirmed on both magic bytes, including when they arrive in separate chunks, so the policy a tail receives does not depend on its first byte or on chunk size.
  • miniz’s assertions are compiled out explicitly. MZ_ASSERT expands to assert() at sites reachable from malformed input, and upstream defines it unconditionally, so its behaviour was left entirely to NDEBUG; a local patch makes it overridable so that a -UNDEBUG build cannot abort() where an ordinary build raises a condition.
  • Match distances are validated against the bytes emitted so far, as RFC 1951 requires, so a malformed stream cannot read outside the decompression window. This is a local patch to the vendored miniz, which performs the check only for a non-wrapping output buffer — a configuration a streaming decoder never uses. Worth knowing if you compare zukomp’s behaviour against stock miniz: zukomp rejects three classes of stream that miniz accepts, all of which RFC 1951 section 3.2.5 forbids.

For package authors

  • A versioned C ABI in inst/include/zukomp.h, reached through zukomp-r.h and R’s registered C-callable mechanism.

  • Other packages can register codecs at ZU_CODEC_VENDOR_BASE. Adding a codec changes no existing declaration and needs no ABI bump. Registration is experimental in this release: zu_register_codec() and zu_codec_vtable are outside the ABI stability promise until a real satellite codec has used them, and may change in a minor release. The core limits apply to a registered codec regardless.

  • zukomp.so exports R_init_zukomp and nothing else (on ELF and Mach-O; Windows exports through R’s .def file). Everything is reached through R’s registration tables, and an exported miniz could otherwise bind to another package’s vendored copy in the same process.

  • ZU_FINISH is delivered to a codec together with the final bytes, not only on a later call with an empty buffer. A codec can therefore tell “these are the last bytes” from “here are some bytes” – which gzip’s next-member probe needs, so that a stream ending in a lone 0x1f is consumed exactly rather than one byte over.

  • Registration enforces codec identity for every registration, declared or not: a declared id must carry its declared name, an undeclared id must be in the vendor range, and names and content-coding tokens must be unique — including against declared codecs whose implementation is absent, whose names are reserved for a satellite to claim with the declared id. The registry is process-global and has no removal API, so one ambiguous registration would otherwise poison codec discovery for the session.

  • A satellite is usable regardless of load order. komp_codecs() caches on a registry mutation counter, so an implementation registered after the table was first read is picked up.

  • zu_codec_vtable, zu_codec_info, zu_encoder_opts and zu_decoder_opts may all gain fields without an ABI bump: each check requires only the prefix the core dereferences, so a consumer compiled against an older header keeps working and simply does not supply the newer fields. Options structs are copied bounded by the caller’s own struct_size, so a shorter one is never read past its end.

  • A second route, for a consumer that needs the ZIP container layer rather than a codec – the members of an .xlsx, for one. An installed zukomp ships lib/libzukomp.a and include/miniz.h, so that layer can be linked through LinkingTo instead of vendoring a second ZIP implementation. The archive is a separate compilation of the vendored miniz.c with the archive APIs left in; zukomp.so keeps exactly the trim it has, and contains no mz_zip_* code at all. The archive’s symbols have hidden visibility too: they link into the consumer as usual, but the consumer’s shared object does not re-export them. See “Using zukomp from C” in the README.

    Resolve it with system.file("lib", .Platform$r_arch, package = "zukomp"). It is architecture-specific object code, so it installs under R_ARCH beside the shared object’s directory – lib/ on every single-arch platform and lib/x64/ on Windows.

    Compile miniz.h with MINIZ_NO_ZLIB_COMPATIBLE_NAMES defined and nothing else. MINIZ_NO_TIME in particular changes MZ_TIME_T, and with it the layout of mz_zip_archive_file_stat, between the consumer’s translation unit and the archive – a silent mismatch rather than a link error.

Notes

  • gzip output is deterministic — no timestamp, no filename — for a fixed zukomp version. It is not a content hash: compressed bytes may change when a vendored codec is updated.
  • Whole-buffer output is built in a realloc’d buffer owned by an R external pointer, so growth releases superseded blocks as it goes and a large decode does not hold several at once.
  • miniz 3.1.2 is vendored and trimmed; provenance is reproducible from tools/vendor/manifest.tsv and verifiable offline with tools/vendor/verify. Its MIT notice is installed at licenses/miniz-LICENSE: miniz.h carries no copyright line of its own, and an installed zukomp ships both that header and compiled miniz code.
  • Deferred to a later release: R-level streaming objects, file and connection helpers, komp_compress_text(), dictionaries, and the brotli/zstd/LZ4/Snappy satellite packages.
